reasoning: Wrote index.html in one pass from reasoning alone; I did not open it in a browser, run it, or use any tool besides the structured output. Design: participants (name, IANA zone, start/end minutes) live in a JSON object encoded in location.hash via history.replaceState; hashchange reloads state. Zones come from Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone') (fallback list if unsupported) fed into a datalist, with loose resolution of city names like 'kolkata' -> Asia/Kolkata; validity checked by constructing Intl.DateTimeFormat. Slots: from the next 30-min boundary, every 30-min UTC instant over 7 days is converted per participant with Intl.DateTimeFormat.formatToParts (hourCycle h23), so half-hour offsets, midnight crossings and DST are handled by the browser's tz data rather than offsets; a slot passes if local minutes m satisfies start<=m and m+30<=end (or the wraparound rule when start>end, e.g. 22:00-06:00). Results are grouped by the viewer's local date, each row showing viewer time range plus each participant's local time, date and zone abbreviation; rows where the viewer/participant offset differs from the previous row on the same day get a dashed 'clock change' marker. Optional viewer-zone override and skip-weekends toggle are also in the hash. Native labelled inputs, buttons, role=status/alert regions, focus rings and a scrollable table give keyboard/phone usability. Known/likely issues since untested: the participant-cell loop computes an unused `end` variable (harmless); clipboard copy needs a secure context; the 'clock change' marker is a heuristic and will not fire if the DST shift happens across a day boundary or a gap in the results; slots at a DST spring-forward gap may be judged by their start minute only; very old browsers without formatToParts/hourCycle are unsupported.
